topic: ai agent tool engineering vs prompt engineering
headline_marked: [[Prompt Engineering is dying]], Tool Engineering is the future
headline: Prompt Engineering is dying, Tool Engineering is the future
summary: As LLMs improve, the need for complex prompts diminishes. Developers must shift focus to building and connecting AI tools.
details: The era of mastering prompt engineering for LLMs is drawing to a close. Skills like few-shot prompting and context window management, once crucial, are becoming obsolete as AI models advance. The future of AI development lies in 'Tool Engineering,' the ability to build, connect, and orchestrate the tools that enable AI agents to interact with the real world.

Several factors are contributing to the decline of prompt engineering. Firstly, LLMs are becoming increasingly adept at understanding natural language, requiring less elaborate prompts for the same results. Secondly, expanded context windows eliminate the need for complex data compression techniques within prompts. Finally, fine-tuning and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) offer more reliable solutions to issues like inconsistent outputs and domain-specific knowledge.

Prompt Engineering was a transitional skill, a workaround for the limitations of early LLMs. As models like GPT-4 and Claude 3 demonstrate superior natural language understanding and instruction following, the specialized skill of prompt engineering is being commoditized. This shift means that the premium salaries and dedicated courses focused on prompt engineering may soon become a thing of the past.

Tool Engineering, in contrast, focuses on giving AI agents the ability to act in the real world. This involves building and connecting tools that allow AI to perform actions like booking flights, querying databases, or sending emails. It requires a solid understanding of APIs, data models, security, and distributed systems, marking a return to traditional engineering principles.

The durability of Tool Engineering is a key advantage. While a prompt can break with model updates, a well-built tool, like a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server, can work with any compatible model. This makes it a compounding investment, unlike prompt engineering techniques that can depreciate with each new model release.

headline_marked: [[Hacked AfD Emails]] Reveal Widespread Antisemitism, Racism, and Violent Fantasies
headline: Hacked AfD Emails Reveal Widespread Antisemitism, Racism, and Violent Fantasies
summary: 281 GB of internal party emails detail racist slurs, antisemitic theories, and disturbing discussions about refugees, alongside alleged financial misconduct.
details: Hackers have released a massive 281 GB archive of 421,179 internal emails from the German political party AfD. The leaked data, published online, provides a stark look into the party's internal communications.

The emails reportedly contain widespread antisemitism, racism, and violent fantasies among party supporters. Examples include racist slurs, antisemitic theories of Jewish world domination, and jokes about processing refugees into handbags and boots.

Further revelations include discussions about shooting refugees at the border and a Christmas card featuring a swastika and "Heil Hitler." One email thread was signed off with "Heil und Sieg," indicating a disturbing embrace of Nazi ideology.

Beyond extremist content, the leaked emails also allegedly point to instances of financial misconduct within the party. The publication aims to provide a clear, unvarnished view of the AfD's internal culture and activities.
